Module 04 · Prompts

Prompts to design and supervise a mission

Use Chat to design and decide; use Sources when the agent must work from a governed corpus with verifiable citations.

View promptsPlaybook
Where to run each prompt

Two interfaces. One clear workflow.

Use Chat to work with sources already in the notebook. Use Sources to find and import new material.

Ask, audit, practise or create

Select the relevant sources and paste the prompt into Chat. NotebookLM answers from that selection and shows citations for review.

How it works in NotebookLM
Find and import evidence

Paste the research question into Sources. Use Fast Research for a quick search or Deep Research for a full briefing. Review results before importing them.

How it works in NotebookLM

You may start in Chat to refine the question. To find and add new sources, finish the step in Sources and then return to Chat.

Prompts

Prompts to design and supervise a mission

WorkflowFrom case to continuity

The prompts move from suitability to contract, permissions, plan, execution and verdict. None performs external actions. In this pilot, no prompt sends, publishes, pays or changes external systems.

Independent use: Use any prompt independently when you provide its declared input artifact; if it is missing, the prompt must ask or stop.

Inputs 1
  • <CASE>process you want to delegateExample: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Select a small, observable and reversible case.
When to use it
Before defining mission or permissions.
Trade-off
A simpler case teaches control before breadth.
Next
Mission brief

Workflow

  • List candidates and intended results.
  • Assess stability, impact and recovery.
  • Recommend one and reject the others with reasons.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Suitability matrix
  • Reversible pilot

Guardrails

  • Reject payments, publishing, sending and sensitive decisions.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • A verdict for every candidate.
  • The case keeps a personal boundary.

Edge cases

  • No case is recoverable.
  • Impact depends on a missing source.

Limits

  • Does not authorize design or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.
1N1 · DirectA clear, concise instruction.
N1Direct

A clear, concise instruction.

Objective: Select a small, observable and reversible case. The final decision and evidence remain under your responsibility.Data: CASE=<CASE · process you want to delegate · e.g.: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources>.Apply: Suitability matrix; Reversible pilot.Order: List candidates and intended results. → Recommend one and reject the others with reasons.Deliver: Suitability matrix; A verdict for every candidate.Boundary: Reject payments, publishing, sending and sensitive decisions.[Flag the missing fact that would change the verdict.]

mission brief

ProducesMission brief
< > replace · [ ] optional · PARAMETERS adjust
Inputs 1
  • <CASE>process you want to delegateExample: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Turn the approved case into a bounded mission with a result, exclusions and a verifiable Definition of Done. You retain final acceptance.
When to use it
After triage and before planning.
Trade-off
More precision limits flexibility but makes the pilot reviewable.
Next
Context package

Workflow

  • Define role, objective and result.
  • Attach context and sources.
  • Document constraints, approval points and the Definition of Done.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Mission Brief (bounded mission contract)
  • Definition of Done (acceptance conditions)

Guardrails

  • Add no implicit permissions.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • Clear objective and exclusions.
  • Mission and Definition of Done are verifiable.

Edge cases

  • Two owners claim the decision.
  • The result cannot be tested.

Limits

  • The brief does not approve the plan or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.

< > replace · [ ] optional · PARAMETERS adjust
Inputs 1
  • <CASE>process you want to delegateExample: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Prepare authorized sources and declare material gaps.
When to use it
Before planning source-dependent steps.
Trade-off
Fewer authorized sources may limit coverage while protecting traceability.
Next
Permission matrix

Workflow

  • Inventory sources, provenance and rights.
  • Link each source to a need.
  • State currency, limits and gaps.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Source inventory
  • Gap log

Guardrails

  • Never fill gaps from memory or conjecture.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every source has use and limit.
  • Every source is within your right to use.

Edge cases

  • Sources conflict.
  • A required source is unavailable.

Limits

  • Does not validate claims unsupported by the sources. Stop when data or authority is missing.
1N1 · DirectA clear, concise instruction.
N1Direct

A clear, concise instruction.

Objective: Prepare authorized sources and declare material gaps. The final decision and evidence remain under your responsibility.Data: CASE=<CASE · process you want to delegate · e.g.: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources>.Apply: Source inventory; Gap log.Order: Inventory sources, provenance and rights. → State currency, limits and gaps.Deliver: Source package and gaps; Every source has use and limit.Boundary: Never fill gaps from memory or conjecture.[Flag the missing fact that would change the verdict.]

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Define what the agent may read, propose or do.
When to use it
After the brief and before instructions.
Trade-off
Narrow permissions require more gates but reduce unintended effects.
Next
Agent instructions

Workflow

  • List data, tools and actions.
  • Classify allowed, approval required or prohibited.
  • Add stop, escalation and revocation.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Least privilege
  • Permission matrix

Guardrails

  • Available access is not authorization.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every capability maps to a step.
  • You can revoke every granted capability.

Edge cases

  • One tool combines read and write.
  • No revocation mechanism exists.

Limits

  • Documents authority; it does not grant it. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Draft invariant instructions with limits and exception response.
When to use it
Once mission, sources and permissions are defined.
Trade-off
Explicit rules reduce improvisation and may require more clarification.
Next

Workflow

  • Order the objective and allowed steps.
  • Include source hierarchy and prohibitions.
  • Define stop, escalation and done.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Instruction hierarchy
  • Stop conditions

Guardrails

  • Invent no tools, data or authority.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • Allowed and prohibited conduct is testable.
  • Instructions preserve your final decision.

Edge cases

  • Two instructions conflict.
  • The output requires a prohibited action.

Limits

  • Produces an instruction draft; it does not activate an agent. Stop when data or authority is missing.

When to use it
Receives
reviewed execution plan
Produces
Plan verdict
Receivesreviewed execution plan
→
ProducesPlan verdict
Action outside NotebookLM

Run the approved plan on an isolated copy outside NotebookLM. Do not send, publish, move, or delete originals. Record input, version, observed output, exceptions, decisions, and recovery.

You must provide
Observed output + execution log
Continue when
Approval matches the executed version, at least one observed output exists, and the log confirms zero external effects. If the test was not run, do not proceed.
< > replace · [ ] optional · PARAMETERS adjust
Inputs 1
  • <CASE>process you want to delegateExample: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Decide whether the proposed plan fits the contract.
When to use it
Before every run, including a pilot.
Trade-off
The gate adds review before effects instead of correction after effects. An approved verdict may support requesting a separate controlled run, but does not perform or authorize it by itself.
Next
Execution audit

Workflow

  • Trace steps to sources and permissions.
  • Review gates, risks and dependencies.
  • Issue approve, correct or reject.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Preflight review
  • Plan gate (human decision point)

Guardrails

  • An approved goal does not validate every step.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • A verdict per criterion.
  • Your verdict identifies the exact plan.

Edge cases

  • The plan omits recovery.
  • A dependency lacks an owner.

Limits

  • The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.

Approved plan v1: verify the copy hash; classify 32 notes; save a preview; reconcile count and uncertainties; leave originals untouched. Recovery: delete the preview. Human approval is bound to this version and case.# Optional adjustmentsFlag the missing fact that would change the verdict.## P — Purpose and scopeExpert role: Act as an agentic operations designer. Preserve human control, traceability and reversibility; stop when data or authority is insufficient.Deliverable: Plan verdictInclude: Decide whether the proposed plan fits the contract.Exclude: The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.## E — Standards and execution### FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- Preflight review- Plan gate (human decision point)Steps:1. Trace steps to sources and permissions.2. Review gates, risks and dependencies.3. Issue approve, correct or reject.### Edge cases- The plan omits recovery.- A dependency lacks an owner.## C — Verifiable criteria# Expected output:- Plan verdict- A verdict per criterion.- Your verdict identifies the exact plan.Observable criteria:- A verdict per criterion.- Your verdict identifies the exact plan.# Definition of Done: A verdict per criterion.; Your verdict identifies the exact plan.Trade-off: The gate adds review before effects instead of correction after effects. An approved verdict may support requesting a separate controlled run, but does not perform or authorize it by itself.## Provenance- Synthetic demo- Declared authorities: module04-official-pdf, m04-validation-points-preserve-control## Metadata- module: 04- prompt: prompt-06- surface: chatReturn conclusions, evidence and auditable metadata; do not expose private reasoning or chain of thought.

Inputs 1
  • <CASE>process you want to delegateExample: prepare a weekly brief from authorized sources · Required
Parameters
  • LENGTH = concise
  • STRUCTURE = short table + verdict
  • DEPTH = executive
Why it worksAcceptance criteria
Purpose
Reconstruct what happened and how exceptions were handled. It consumes the log from a separate controlled run; this prompt does not execute the plan.
When to use it
After a controlled run or when reviewing a log.
Trade-off
Logging takes time and makes the case reviewable.
Next
Pilot review

Workflow

  • Order inputs, version and plan.
  • Link decisions, gates and actions.
  • Compare output, exceptions and done.

Best practices and frameworks

  • Execution Log (versioned run record)
  • Exception taxonomy

Guardrails

  • Never treat an absent record as success.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every decision has evidence.
  • The log comes from a separate controlled run.

Edge cases

  • Part of the log is missing.
  • The result looks right but broke a limit.

Limits

  • Infers no cause or performance beyond evidence. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Workflow

  • Summarize compliance and deviations.
  • Assess corrections and limits.
  • Issue verdict, owner and next gate.

Best practices and frameworks

  • After Action Review (AAR; post-action review)
  • Keep–Adjust–Stop

Guardrails

  • Do not widen scope to compensate for failure.
  • Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Acceptance criteria

  • One decision with reason.
  • Continuity respects your original boundary.

Edge cases

  • Evidence is insufficient.
  • The case passed but the next context changes permissions.

Limits

  • Does not authorize a new context or external effect. Stop when data or authority is missing.

From doing to orchestrating

Delegate a process without giving up your judgment.

Giving an AI a vague goal can accelerate the wrong outcome. Useful autonomy begins by stating what it may decide, what it must escalate and how success is checked.

What you will produce

You finish with a mission brief, permission matrix, approved plan and the record of one small, reversible run.

How to proceed

Choose a case, design the contract, limit tools, approve the plan, observe execution and decide whether to keep, adjust or stop.

What to verify

Keep the brief, approved plan, exceptions, sources used, result and final decision.

Design my pilot

Expand autonomy only after the pilot passes; otherwise adjust or stop.
